recipes.title: Banana Peanut-Butter Oatmeal
steps: Bring milk to a simmer, stir in oats.
Cook 5–6 min, stirring, until creamy.
Mash one banana into the pot; slice the other on top.
Swirl in peanut butter and cinnamon; drizzle honey for the kids.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Serve slightly cooled; let kids add their own banana slices.

recipes.title: Vegetable Poha
steps: Rinse poha in a sieve until soft; drain.
Heat oil; pop mustard seeds, add curry leaves, onion; fry 2 min.
Add diced potato + peas, turmeric, salt; cover 5 min until soft.
Fold in poha, warm 2 min, squeeze lemon, top with cilantro.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Skip green chili; peanuts on the side for the 4-year-old.

recipes.title: Besan Chilla (Savory Chickpea Pancakes)

ingredients.note: carom seeds — they make besan easier to digest

steps: Sift 200 g besan into a bowl with ½ tsp turmeric, ¾ tsp ground cumin, ¼ tsp chilli powder, ½ tsp ajwain and 1 tsp salt.
Add 250 ml water a little at a time, whisking, until the batter is smooth and about as thick as double cream. Lumps now become lumps in the pan.
Rest the batter for 10 minutes. Besan absorbs water as it sits, so check it again after resting and loosen with a splash if needed.
Stir in the finely chopped onion, tomato, pepper, grated ginger and coriander. Chop everything small; big pieces tear the chilla when you flip it.
Heat a non-stick tawa on medium until a drop of water dances on it. Rub it with a little oil using a folded paper towel.
Pour a ladleful of batter and spread it outwards in a spiral with the back of the ladle to about 15 cm.
Drizzle ½ tsp oil around the edge and cook for 2–3 minutes, until the top looks dry and the edges lift away from the pan.
Flip and cook the second side for 1½–2 minutes, pressing lightly, until both sides are golden with brown freckles.
Keep the cooked chillas in a covered plate while you make the rest — they stay soft.
Serve hot with yogurt or ketchup, cut into strips for small hands.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Make them small — three little chillas beat one big one — and let a child dip them in yogurt or ketchup. Grate the vegetables so nothing is recognisable.
recipes.sourceNote: Written for Rasoi — the standard besan batter, rested and thinned to a coating

recipes.title: Vegetable Sooji Upma
steps: Dry-roast sooji 4 min until fragrant; set aside.
Heat ghee; pop mustard seeds, add ginger, onion, curry leaves.
Add carrot, peas and 600 ml water; salt; boil.
Stream in sooji while stirring; cover 3 min off heat.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Add a spoon of ghee and a squeeze of lemon; kids like it shaped into balls.

recipes.title: Instant Pot Idli with Coconut Chutney
steps: (Batter: soak rice + dal 6 h, grind in Vitamix, ferment overnight in Instant Pot on Yogurt mode 8 h.)
Grease idli molds, fill, steam 12 min in Instant Pot (vent open).
Blend coconut, roasted chana, ginger, salt and 100 ml water in Vitamix for chutney.
Serve warm with chutney.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Soft, mild, hand-held — a reliable favourite; keep chutney mild.

recipes.title: Cheesy Veggie Egg Scramble
steps: Melt butter; soften diced pepper 2 min; wilt spinach 1 min.
Pour in whisked eggs with a pinch of salt; stir gently over low heat.
Fold in cheese when just set.
Serve on toasted bread.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Chop veg small; kids can pick 'their' toppings.

recipes.title: Moong Dal Chilla with Paneer Filling
steps: (Soak moong dal 3 h.) Blend with ginger, cumin, salt and water in Vitamix to a thin batter.
Spread on a hot oiled pan, cook 2 min per side.
Crumble paneer with cilantro; spoon inside and fold.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: High-protein 'dosa' the kids can roll and eat by hand.

recipes.title: Overnight Berry Chia Oats
steps: Mix oats, chia, milk, yogurt in jars.
Top with berries; refrigerate overnight.
Stir and eat cold or warmed 1 min.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Let each kid build their own jar the night before.

recipes.title: Ragi Banana Pancakes
steps: Mash bananas; whisk with milk and jaggery.
Stir in flours and baking powder to a thick batter.
Cook small pancakes in ghee 2 min per side.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Naturally sweet; add a few chocolate chips on the 9-year-old's.

recipes.title: Avocado Toast with Boiled Egg
steps: Boil eggs 9 min; cool and slice.
Mash avocado with lemon and salt.
Toast bread; spread avocado; top with egg and tomato.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Cut into 'soldiers' for the little one.

recipes.title: Vermicelli Upma with Vegetables
steps: Roast vermicelli dry 3 min; set aside.
Temper mustard seeds in oil; sauté onion, carrot, peas.
Add 400 ml water + salt; boil; add vermicelli; cover 4 min.
Finish with lemon.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Noodle-shaped breakfast — kids eat it with a fork happily.

recipes.title: Savory Masala Oats
steps: Sizzle cumin in oil; sauté onion, tomato, peas 3 min.
Add oats + 500 ml water, turmeric, salt; simmer 5 min.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Top with a spoon of yogurt to cool it and soften flavours.

recipes.title: Instant Pot Vegetable Khichdi

ingredients.note: ¾ cup, rinsed with the rice
one for cooking, one to finish
instead of chilli, for young children

steps: Rinse 150 g rice and 150 g moong dal together in three changes of water until it runs almost clear.
Set the Instant Pot to Sauté and warm 1 tbsp ghee. Add ¾ tsp cumin seeds and a pinch of asafoetida and wait 20 seconds for them to sizzle.
Add the chopped onion and fry 4 minutes until soft and just golden.
Stir in 1 tsp grated ginger, then the tomato and diced carrot. Cook 3 minutes.
Add the drained rice and dal, ½ tsp turmeric, 1½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp black pepper. Stir once to coat.
Pour in 1 litre water — khichdi wants roughly 1 part grains to 3½ parts water, softer than plain rice.
Cancel Sauté, close the lid and pressure cook on high for 8 minutes, then let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes. On the stovetop: 3 whistles on medium.
Open the pot and stir in the frozen peas; the residual heat cooks them in 2 minutes and keeps them green.
Stir well, mashing a little against the side of the pot. If it is stiffer than you like, beat in hot water 50 ml at a time — it thickens as it stands.
Finish with the last 1 tbsp ghee and the chopped coriander, and serve with lemon wedges and yogurt.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: The most forgiving meal in the app: soft, mild and one bowl. A spoon of ghee on top at the table is what children remember about it.
recipes.sourceNote: Adapted from Swasthi's Dal Khichdi (Indian Healthy Recipes)

recipes.title: Instant Pot Toor Dal Fry with Rice

ingredients.note: 1 cup, rinsed in three changes of water
Kashmiri, for colour rather than heat
level, plus a pinch for the rice

steps: Rinse 200 g toor dal in three changes of water, rubbing the grains between your fingers until the water runs almost clear. This is what keeps the dal from tasting muddy.

Put the dal in the Instant Pot with 600 ml water and ¼ tsp of the turmeric. Pressure cook on high for 8 minutes, then let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes. On the stovetop: 3 whistles on medium, then leave it alone until the pressure drops.

While the dal cooks, rinse 300 g basmati rice until the water is clear, then simmer it in 600 ml water with a pinch of salt: 12 minutes covered on low, then 5 minutes off the heat without lifting the lid.
Open the pot and whisk the dal for a few seconds. It should be soft enough to fall off the whisk in ribbons; if it is stiff, whisk in 100 ml hot water. Tip it into a bowl and wipe the pot dry.
Set the pot to Sauté (or use a kadai on medium). Warm 2 tbsp ghee, add ¾ tsp cumin seeds and wait for them to darken by a shade and smell toasted — about 20 seconds.

Add ⅛ tsp asafoetida and the slit green chilli, then the chopped onion. Fry for 5–6 minutes, stirring often, until the onion is golden at the edges. Do not rush this; pale onion is the usual reason dal tastes flat.
Stir in 1 tsp grated ginger and 1 tsp minced garlic and fry for 45 seconds, until the raw smell goes.
Add the chopped tomato and ½ tsp of the salt. Cook for 5–6 minutes, mashing with the back of the spoon, until the tomato collapses and the ghee separates at the edges.
Turn the heat low and add ¼ tsp turmeric, ½ tsp red chilli powder and 1 tsp coriander powder. Fry for 60 seconds — off the boil, so the spices bloom instead of burning.

Pour the dal back in with the remaining ¾ tsp salt. Simmer uncovered for 6–8 minutes, stirring now and then, adding hot water a splash at a time until it pours like thin cream — it thickens as it sits.
Turn off the heat. Crush 1 tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the pot, add ½ tsp garam masala and the chopped coriander, and stir once.
Lift out the green chilli. Taste and adjust the salt, then serve over the rice with lemon wedges on the side.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Keep the green chilli whole and lift it out before serving, and put a spoon of ghee and a lemon wedge on the table so each child can finish their own bowl.
recipes.sourceNote: Adapted from Swasthi's Dal Fry (Indian Healthy Recipes)

recipes.title: Instant Pot Rajma Chawal

ingredients.note: 1 cup, soaked 8 hours in plenty of cold water

steps: The night before, rinse 200 g rajma and soak it in 1 litre of cold water. Eight hours is the minimum; beans that have not soaked stay chalky however long you cook them.
Drain the soaking water and rinse the beans again — this is what makes them easier on everyone's stomach.

Pressure cook the beans in 400 ml fresh water for 16 minutes on high with a natural release, or 5 whistles on the stovetop. A cooked bean squashes to a paste between two fingers with no grit in the middle.
Meanwhile rinse 300 g basmati rice until the water runs clear and simmer in 600 ml water with a pinch of salt: 12 minutes covered on low, then 5 minutes resting off the heat.
Lift the beans out with a slotted spoon and keep the cooking liquid — it is the body of the gravy. Set the pot to Sauté.
Warm 2 tbsp ghee, add ½ tsp cumin seeds and the bay leaf, and wait 20 seconds for the seeds to sizzle and smell toasted.
Add the chopped onion and fry for 8–9 minutes, stirring often, until it is properly golden — not just soft. This is the single step that decides how the dish tastes.
Stir in 1 tsp grated ginger and 1½ tsp minced garlic; fry 1 minute until the raw edge is gone.
Pour in the tomato purée and ½ tsp salt. Cook for 6–8 minutes, until it darkens, thickens and the ghee separates out at the sides.
Lower the heat and add ¼ tsp turmeric, ½ tsp chilli powder, 2 tsp coriander powder and 1 tsp ground cumin. Fry for 2 minutes, adding a spoon of water if the pan looks dry.
Add the beans, 250 ml of their cooking liquid and the remaining 1 tsp salt. Simmer uncovered for 12–15 minutes.
Mash about a quarter of the beans against the side of the pot with the back of a ladle. The gravy should coat a spoon rather than run off it.
Turn off the heat, crush 1 tbsp kasuri methi between your palms into the pot, add ¾ tsp garam masala and the coriander, and stir once.
Let it sit for 5 minutes before serving over the rice — rajma is better five minutes late than five minutes early.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Mash a few beans against the side of the pot so the gravy is thick and easy to eat with a spoon, and keep the chilli powder at ½ tsp — the flavour is in the onion and the kasuri methi, not the heat.
recipes.sourceNote: Adapted from Swasthi's Rajma Masala (Indian Healthy Recipes)

recipes.title: Instant Pot Chole (Mild Chickpea Curry)
steps: Soak 200 g dried chickpeas in 1 litre of water for at least 8 hours, or overnight. Drain and rinse.
Pressure cook them in 400 ml fresh water for 18 minutes on high with a natural release (5–6 whistles on the stovetop). A cooked chickpea mashes completely with no hard core.
Scoop the chickpeas out, keeping the cooking stock. Set the pot to Sauté and warm 2 tbsp oil.
Add the bay leaf, cinnamon and cloves and let them sizzle for 20 seconds — this is where the warm background flavour comes from.
Add the chopped onion and fry for 8–9 minutes to a proper golden brown, stirring so the edges do not catch.
Stir in 1 tsp ginger and 1½ tsp garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and ¾ tsp salt. Cook for 6–7 minutes, pressing them down, until they are mushy and the oil beads at the edge of the pan.
Turn the heat low. Add ¼ tsp turmeric, 1 tsp chilli powder, 2 tsp coriander powder and ½ tsp ground cumin, and fry for 3 minutes until the mixture smells sweet rather than raw.
Add the chickpeas, 300 ml of their stock and the remaining ¾ tsp salt. Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, until the gravy is thick enough to sit on a spoon.
Crush a ladleful of chickpeas against the side of the pot to thicken the gravy naturally.
Turn off the heat and stir in 1 tsp garam masala, ½ tsp amchur and 1 tsp crushed kasuri methi. Taste: it should be tangy first, warm second.
Scatter the coriander over and let it stand 5 minutes before serving.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Serve with plain rice or a soft roti and a bowl of yogurt; the amchur at the end gives the tang children expect from chole without any extra chilli.
recipes.sourceNote: Adapted from Swasthi's Chana Masala (Indian Healthy Recipes)

recipes.title: Palak Paneer (Vitamix-smooth)
steps: Bring a wide pan of water to the boil with ½ tsp salt. Have a bowl of iced water ready beside it.
Drop the spinach into the boiling water for exactly 2 minutes, then lift it straight into the iced water. The shock is what keeps the finished dish green instead of grey.
Squeeze the spinach lightly and blend it with the cashews, the green chilli if you are using it, and 60 ml water until completely smooth — 30 seconds on high in a Vitamix. Set the purée aside.
Cut 250 g paneer into 2 cm cubes. If it has been in the fridge, soak the cubes in hot water for 10 minutes so they stay soft in the curry.
Warm 1 tbsp oil with 1 tbsp butter in a wide pan. Add ½ tsp cumin seeds and let them crackle for 20 seconds.
Add the chopped onion and fry for 5–6 minutes until golden at the edges.
Stir in ¾ tsp ginger and ¾ tsp garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the deseeded tomato and ½ tsp salt and cook for 4–5 minutes, until soft and jammy.
Sprinkle in ¾ tsp garam masala and fry for 1 minute.
Turn the heat to low and pour in the spinach purée with 100 ml water and the remaining ½ tsp salt. Cook for just 3 minutes — long boiling is what dulls the colour.
Slide in the paneer, crush ½ tsp kasuri methi over the pan and stir gently so the cubes stay whole. Cook 2 minutes more.
Turn off the heat, swirl in the milk or cream if using, and serve straight away with roti or rice.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Blanching and shocking the spinach keeps it bright green rather than khaki, which matters more to children than anything else on the plate. Leave the chilli out and add a spoon of cream at the end.
recipes.sourceNote: Adapted from Swasthi's Palak Paneer (Indian Healthy Recipes)

recipes.title: Matar Paneer

ingredients.note: about 20 g — this is what makes it creamy

steps: Warm 1 tbsp oil in a pan and fry the cubed onion for 5–6 minutes until golden at the edges.
Add the tomatoes, cashews, ginger, garlic and ½ tsp salt. Cover and cook for 8 minutes, until the tomatoes are collapsing and the cashews are soft enough to blend.
Let it cool for a few minutes, then blend to a completely smooth paste — 30 seconds on high. Straining it through a sieve is optional but gives a restaurant texture.
Cut 250 g paneer into 2 cm cubes and soak them in hot water while you make the gravy; they stay soft instead of squeaky.
Warm 1½ tbsp ghee in the same pan. Add ½ tsp cumin seeds and let them crackle for 20 seconds.
Turn the heat low and add ¼ tsp turmeric, ¾ tsp chilli powder and 1 tsp coriander powder. Fry for 30 seconds — low heat, or ground spices scorch and turn bitter.
Pour in the blended paste (it will spit, so stand back) and cook for 3–4 minutes on medium, stirring, until it thickens and the ghee shows at the edges.
Add 250 ml water, 160 g frozen peas and the remaining ¾ tsp salt. Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, until the peas are tender and the gravy coats a spoon.
If you are using yogurt, take the pan off the heat and whisk it in a spoonful at a time so it cannot split, then return to a low heat.
Drain the paneer and slide it in. Crush 1 tsp kasuri methi over the pan, add ½ tsp garam masala and simmer for just 2 minutes — longer makes paneer rubbery.
Scatter the coriander over and serve with roti, naan or plain rice.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Blending the base makes it smooth, so there are no chunks of onion to argue with. Frozen peas straight from the bag keep their sweetness and their colour.
recipes.sourceNote: Adapted from Swasthi's Matar Paneer (Indian Healthy Recipes)

recipes.title: Aloo Gobi (Potato & Cauliflower Stir-Fry)

ingredients.note: about half a head, in 4 cm florets

steps: Cut the potatoes into 2 cm cubes and keep them in a bowl of water so they do not brown. Break the cauliflower into 4 cm florets.
Soak the florets in hot water for 3–4 minutes, then drain them well and pat dry. Wet cauliflower steams instead of frying, and steamed cauliflower is what goes soggy.
Heat 2½ tbsp oil in a wide, heavy pan on medium. Add ½ tsp cumin seeds and wait for them to sizzle.
Add the ginger, garlic and green chilli; fry 30 seconds. Add the onion and cook 4–5 minutes until translucent and just turning gold.
Drain the potatoes and add them. Stir-fry 3 minutes, then cover and cook 8–9 minutes on low, stirring twice, until half done. Add a tablespoon of water only if they catch.
Add the cauliflower and stir-fry uncovered for 3 minutes, letting a few florets brown — that browning is most of the flavour.
Sprinkle in ¼ tsp turmeric, ¾ tsp chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder and ½ tsp roasted cumin. Toss to coat, then sprinkle 2 tbsp water around the sides of the pan.
Cover and cook on low for 6–8 minutes, stirring gently every couple of minutes, until a potato cube gives easily to a knife but the cauliflower still has a slight crunch.
Now add 1 tsp salt and the chopped tomatoes. Salt earlier draws water out and softens the cauliflower too far.
Raise the heat and stir-fry uncovered for 2–3 minutes until the tomato loses its raw smell and clings to the vegetables.
Turn off the heat. Crush 1 tbsp kasuri methi over the pan, add 1 tsp garam masala and ½ tsp amchur, and fold through once.
Finish with the chopped coriander and serve with roti or as a side with dal and rice.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Cut the potato small so it cooks through, and stop while the cauliflower still has a little bite — children reject it once it goes soft and grey.
recipes.sourceNote: Adapted from Swasthi's Aloo Gobi (Indian Healthy Recipes)

recipes.title: Instant Pot Dal Palak (Spinach Lentils)
steps: Rinse 100 g moong dal and 100 g masoor dal together until the water runs clear — three changes is usually enough.
Pressure cook the dals with 600 ml water and ¼ tsp turmeric: 8 minutes on high with a 10-minute natural release, or 2 whistles on the stovetop.
While that cooks, wash the spinach well and chop it small — stems and all, as long as they are tender.
Open the pot and whisk the dal briefly; it should be soft and pourable. Tip it into a bowl.
Set the pot to Sauté and warm 1½ tbsp ghee. Add ¾ tsp cumin seeds and let them crackle for 20 seconds.
Add a pinch of asafoetida, then the sliced garlic. Fry for 1 minute until the garlic is pale gold — it turns bitter the moment it goes brown.
Add the grated ginger and the slit chilli, then the chopped tomato and ½ tsp of the salt. Cook 4 minutes until the tomato softens.
Add the spinach in handfuls, stirring as it wilts. Two to three minutes is plenty; long cooking turns it grey.
Pour the dal back in with the remaining ¾ tsp salt and 100 ml hot water. Simmer for 5 minutes so the flavours meet.
Turn off the heat, stir in 1 tbsp lemon juice and the coriander, and lift out the green chilli.
Serve with rice or roti. It thickens as it stands, so keep a little hot water by the stove to loosen it.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Chop the spinach small so it disappears into the dal, and finish with lemon — the sourness is what makes children come back for a second bowl.
recipes.sourceNote: Adapted from Swasthi's Dal Palak (Indian Healthy Recipes)

recipes.title: Instant Pot Vegetable Pulao + Raita
steps: Rinse 300 g basmati rice until the water runs clear, then soak it for 20 minutes and drain well. Soaked rice cooks into separate grains; unsoaked rice clumps.
Set the Instant Pot to Sauté and warm 2 tbsp ghee.
Add the bay leaf, cinnamon, cardamom pods, cloves and ¾ tsp cumin seeds. Wait about 30 seconds, until they smell fragrant and the cumin darkens a shade.
Add the sliced onion and fry for 4–5 minutes until golden at the edges.
Stir in 1 tsp ginger, 1 tsp garlic and the slit chilli; cook 1 minute.
Add the mixed vegetables and the mint leaves and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the drained rice and turn it over gently two or three times to coat it in the ghee — gently, or the soaked grains break.
Pour in 420 ml water and add 1¼ tsp salt. Taste the water: it should be a little saltier than you want the finished rice.
Cancel Sauté, close the lid and pressure cook on high for 5 minutes, then let the pressure release naturally for 5 minutes before opening.
While it cooks, make the raita: whisk 300 g yogurt smooth, stir in the grated and squeezed cucumber, ½ tsp roasted cumin and a pinch of salt.
Open the pot, lift the rice with a fork rather than stirring it, and let it stand uncovered for 5 minutes so the grains firm up.
Serve with the raita, pushing the whole spices aside as you spoon it out.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Whole spices are for flavour, not for eating — push the cinnamon and cardamom to the side of the pot as you serve. The cool raita is what makes it a whole meal.
recipes.sourceNote: Adapted from Swasthi's Veg Pulao (Indian Healthy Recipes)

recipes.title: Pav Bhaji (Vegetable Mash with Buns)

ingredients.note: large, finely chopped, plus extra raw to serve
two for the bhaji, one for the pav

steps: Pressure cook the diced potato, cauliflower, carrot and peas with 350 ml water for 4 minutes on high (1–2 whistles on the stovetop), until everything is completely soft.
Drain, keeping the cooking water, and mash the vegetables roughly with a potato masher. Leave some texture — this is a mash, not a purée.
Warm 2 tbsp butter with 1 tbsp oil in a wide pan. Fry the chopped onion for 5 minutes until translucent.
Add the grated ginger and minced garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add the chopped bell pepper and fry 3–4 minutes until it softens.
Add the tomatoes and ¾ tsp of the salt and cook 6–7 minutes, pressing them down, until they are completely mushy and the butter separates.
Turn the heat low and add 1½ tbsp pav bhaji masala, 1 tsp chilli powder and ¼ tsp turmeric. Fry for 2 minutes.
Add the mashed vegetables and 150 ml of the reserved cooking water with the remaining ½ tsp salt. Mash again in the pan and simmer for 5 minutes.
Keep mashing and stirring as it simmers; the bhaji is ready when it is thick, glossy and a deep red-brown, about 8 minutes in total.
Crush ¾ tbsp kasuri methi over the pan and stir through.
Slit the pav almost in half. Melt the last 1 tbsp butter on a griddle, sprinkle a pinch of pav bhaji masala into it, and toast the cut sides for 1–2 minutes until lightly crisp.
Serve the bhaji with a knob of butter on top, the toasted pav, raw chopped onion, coriander and lemon wedges.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: This is the most reliable way to get four vegetables into a child in one bowl. Toast the pav in butter — the buttered bun is half the appeal — and keep the chilli powder to 1 tsp.
recipes.sourceNote: Adapted from Swasthi's Pav Bhaji (Indian Healthy Recipes)

recipes.title: Instant Pot Sambar with Rice

ingredients.note: or a lime-sized ball soaked in 120 ml hot water
the traditional balance to the tamarind

steps: Rinse 200 g toor dal until the water runs clear, then pressure cook it with 600 ml water and ¼ tsp turmeric: 8 minutes on high with natural release, or 3 whistles.
Rinse 300 g rice and simmer it in 600 ml water with a pinch of salt: 12 minutes covered on low, then 5 minutes off the heat.
Whisk the cooked dal smooth with a ladle and set it aside.

In the same pot on Sauté, add 400 ml water, the carrot, bottle gourd, beans, onion and tomato with ¼ tsp turmeric and 1 tsp of the salt. Simmer 8–10 minutes until the vegetables are tender but still holding their shape.
Stir 1½ tsp tamarind paste into 120 ml hot water and add it to the pot. Simmer 5 minutes — cooking off the raw tamarind is what stops sambar tasting harsh.
Add 2 tbsp sambar powder and the remaining ½ tsp salt, and simmer another 3 minutes.
Pour in the whisked dal with 200 ml hot water. Sambar should pour easily from a ladle; add more hot water if it does not.
Simmer gently for 5 minutes, then stir in 1 tsp jaggery if you are using it and taste. It should read sour, then salty, then sweet in the background.
For the tempering, heat 1½ tbsp ghee in a small pan. Add 1 tsp mustard seeds and wait for them to pop, then ½ tsp cumin seeds, the broken chillies and the curry leaves.
As soon as the curry leaves crackle — about 15 seconds — add ¼ tsp asafoetida and pour the whole thing into the sambar. Cover for a minute to trap the aroma.
Stir in the coriander and serve over the rice, with the remaining sambar in a bowl for second helpings.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Sambar is sour and savoury rather than hot. Ladle it thin over rice with a spoon of ghee, and keep the vegetables in big enough pieces to pick out if a child wants to.
recipes.sourceNote: Written for Rasoi — the standard South Indian toor dal and tamarind method

recipes.title: Paneer Frankie Wraps

ingredients.note: medium: half sliced for the filling, half raw for the top
sprinkled at the end — this is the frankie flavour

steps: Cut 300 g paneer into 1 cm batons and toss them with 3 tbsp yogurt, ¼ tsp turmeric, ½ tsp chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp ginger, 1 tsp garlic and ½ tsp salt. Leave for 10 minutes while you cut the vegetables.
Slice half the onion, the bell pepper and the cabbage as thinly as you can — thin slices cook in the time the paneer takes and stay crunchy in the wrap.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide pan on medium-high. Add the paneer in a single layer and leave it alone for 2 minutes so it browns before you turn it.
Turn the pieces, cook 2 minutes more, then lift them out. Overcooked paneer goes squeaky.
Add the last 1 tbsp oil to the pan with the sliced onion and pepper. Stir-fry 3 minutes on high — you want colour on the edges and bite in the middle.
Add the cabbage and the remaining ½ tsp salt and stir-fry 1 minute.
Return the paneer, add ½ tsp garam masala and squeeze over the lemon. Toss once and turn the heat off.
Warm the tortillas one at a time on a dry tawa, about 30 seconds a side, until soft and flexible but not crisp.
Spread each tortilla with ketchup or green chutney, spoon the filling down the middle, and scatter raw onion, coriander and ¼ tsp chaat masala over it.
Roll tightly, wrap the bottom half in foil or greaseproof paper, and serve while the paneer is still warm.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Wraps beat plates. Let each child build their own and roll it in foil or paper so they can hold it — and keep the chaat masala on the table rather than in the pan.
recipes.sourceNote: Written for Rasoi — the Mumbai street-style frankie, made on a tawa

recipes.title: Instant Pot Vegetable Biryani (Mild)

ingredients.note: two for frying the onion, one to finish

steps: Rinse 300 g basmati until the water runs clear, soak 20 minutes, then drain in a sieve for 10 minutes. Draining matters — wet rice makes a claggy biryani.

Mix the frozen vegetables and paneer with 150 g yogurt, ½ tbsp of the ginger, ½ tbsp of the garlic, ¼ tsp turmeric, ½ tsp chilli powder, ½ tsp garam masala and ½ tsp salt. Leave to marinate while you fry the onions.
Set the Instant Pot to Sauté and heat 2 tbsp ghee. Fry the sliced onions for 8–10 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden. Take half out and keep them for the top.
To the onions in the pot add the bay leaf, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves and ¾ tsp cumin seeds and let them sizzle 30 seconds.
Add the remaining ginger and garlic and the slit chilli; cook 1 minute.
Tip in the marinated vegetables and cook on Sauté for 4 minutes, until the yogurt thickens and clings rather than pooling.
Add half the mint and coriander and stir through.
Spread the drained rice on top in an even layer and pour over 420 ml water with the remaining 1 tsp salt. Do not stir — the rice should sit above the masala.
Cancel Sauté, close the lid and pressure cook on high for 5 minutes, then let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes.
Open the pot, drizzle over the last 1 tbsp ghee and 1 tbsp lemon juice, and fold once or twice with a fork — folding, not stirring, keeps the grains whole.
Scatter the reserved fried onions and the rest of the mint and coriander over the top and let it stand 5 minutes before serving with raita.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: A one-pot biryani rather than a layered one, so it is quick and everything is soft. Mint and yogurt do the work that chilli usually does.
recipes.sourceNote: Written for Rasoi — one-pot pressure-cooker method with a yogurt marinade

recipes.title: Instant Pot Kadhi with Rice

ingredients.note: sour is better here; whisked smooth

steps: Whisk 400 g yogurt with 6 tbsp besan and 600 ml water until there is not a single lump. A minute with a balloon whisk, or 20 seconds in a blender.
Rinse 300 g rice until clear and simmer in 600 ml water with a pinch of salt: 12 minutes covered on low, then 5 minutes off the heat.
Set the Instant Pot to Sauté and warm 2 tbsp ghee. Add ¾ tsp cumin and ½ tsp mustard seeds and wait for the mustard to pop.
Add a pinch of asafoetida, the broken red chillies and the curry leaves; stand back, they spit.
Add the chopped onion and fry 4 minutes until soft, then the grated ginger for 1 minute.
Turn the heat to low and pour in the yogurt mixture with ½ tsp turmeric and 1¼ tsp salt.
Stir constantly until it comes to a simmer. This is the step that matters: unstirred yogurt splits, and split kadhi never comes back together.
Once it simmers, cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes, stirring every couple of minutes, until it thickens enough to coat the spoon and the raw besan taste is gone.
Taste and adjust the salt; add a little hot water if it has gone past pouring consistency.
Lift out the dried chillies, stir in the coriander, and ladle over the rice.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Kadhi is tangy rather than spicy, and children usually like it poured over plain rice. Whisk the yogurt and besan really smooth so there are no lumps to find.
recipes.sourceNote: Written for Rasoi — the classic Punjabi besan-and-yogurt method

recipes.title: Methi Thepla with Yogurt

ingredients.note: about 100 g, leaves only, finely chopped
½ cup, plus more to serve
1 in the dough, the rest for cooking

steps: Pick the methi leaves off their stems — the stems are where most of the bitterness sits — wash them well and chop finely. You want about 1 packed cup.
In a wide bowl mix 300 g atta, the chopped methi, ½ tsp turmeric, ½ tsp chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, ½ tsp cumin, 1 tsp grated ginger, 1 tsp salt, ½ tsp sugar and the sesame seeds.
Add 120 g yogurt and 1 tbsp oil and rub everything together with your fingers until it looks like damp breadcrumbs.
Add water a tablespoon at a time — usually 60–90 ml — and knead for 4–5 minutes into a soft dough, softer than you would make for roti. The methi keeps releasing water, so go slowly.
Cover the dough and rest it for 15 minutes. Rested dough rolls thin without tearing.
Divide into 12 balls. Roll each one out to about 15 cm, dusting with flour as needed.
Heat a tawa on medium until a drop of water skitters across it.
Cook a thepla for 30 seconds, until small bubbles appear, then flip.
Brush the top with oil, flip again, and press the edges down with a folded cloth so it puffs. Cook until both sides have brown freckles — about 2 minutes in total.
Stack the cooked thepla in a covered container or wrapped in a cloth; trapped steam is what keeps them soft.
Serve warm with thick yogurt, and pack the leftovers cold for lunch the next day.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Thepla are soft when made with yogurt in the dough and stay soft in a lunchbox. Chop the methi finely so the bitterness is spread thin.
recipes.sourceNote: Written for Rasoi — the standard Gujarati yogurt-dough method

recipes.title: Black Bean & Cheese Quesadillas
steps: Warm 1 tbsp olive oil in a pan and cook the onion and pepper for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, 1 tsp ground cumin and 1 tsp taco seasoning and cook 1 minute.
Add the drained beans, the corn, ¾ tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper, and cook 3 minutes.
Mash about half the beans against the side of the pan. Half-mashed is the right texture: it holds together without turning into a paste.
Squeeze in the lime juice, stir in the coriander, and take the pan off the heat.
Lay a tortilla in a dry pan over medium heat. Scatter a quarter of the cheese over half of it, spoon a quarter of the bean mixture on top, and fold the tortilla over.
Cook for 2–3 minutes, pressing down with a spatula, until the underside has brown spots.
Flip carefully and cook the second side for 2 minutes, until the cheese has melted all the way through.
Slide onto a board and let it sit for a minute before cutting — cutting straight away makes the filling run out.
Cut into triangles and serve with salsa and sour cream for dipping.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Cut into triangles and let them dip. Mashing half the beans stops the filling falling out of the first bite, which is what usually causes the complaints.
recipes.sourceNote: Written for Rasoi — dry-pan method so the tortilla crisps rather than fries

recipes.title: Build-Your-Own Veggie Tacos

ingredients.note: 1½ for the vegetables, ½ for the beans

steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan).
Toss the diced sweet potato, peppers and onion with 2 tbsp olive oil, 1½ tsp ground cumin, 2 tsp taco seasoning and ¾ tsp salt.
Spread on a lined tray in a single layer — crowded vegetables steam instead of roasting — and roast 20 minutes, turning once, until the edges are browned.
Meanwhile warm the beans in a small pan with ½ tsp cumin, ½ tsp salt and 3 tbsp water, mashing a few against the side, for 5 minutes.
Prepare the cold toppings while the tray is in the oven: shred the lettuce, dice the tomatoes, slice the avocado, grate the cheese, chop the coriander.
Warm the tortillas one at a time in a dry pan, 20 seconds a side, and stack them under a clean cloth so they stay soft and pliable.
Put everything on the table in its own bowl, with lime wedges.
Squeeze lime over the roasted vegetables just before serving — it lifts the whole tray.
Let everyone build their own: beans first, then vegetables, then the cold toppings.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Everything in separate bowls, everyone builds their own. Choosing what goes in is the reason children eat vegetables at a taco dinner and not at any other.
recipes.sourceNote: Written for Rasoi — roasted vegetables and spiced beans, assembled at the table

recipes.title: Burrito Bowls with Cilantro-Lime Rice

ingredients.note: juice of one, wedges from the other
chopped, most of it into the rice

steps: Rinse 300 g rice until the water runs clear and cook it in 600 ml water with ½ tsp salt: 12 minutes covered on low, then 5 minutes off the heat without lifting the lid.
While the rice cooks, heat 1 tbsp olive oil and fry the sliced onion and pepper on high for 5 minutes, so they take on colour rather than just softening.
Add the garlic, 1 tsp of the cumin, 1 tsp taco seasoning and ½ tsp salt and cook 1 minute. Tip into a bowl.
In the same pan warm the beans and corn with ½ tsp cumin, ½ tsp salt and 2 tbsp water for 4 minutes.
Fluff the cooked rice with a fork, then fold in the juice of one lime, most of the chopped coriander and 1 tbsp olive oil. Doing this off the heat keeps the coriander green.
Taste the rice: it should be bright and a little salty on its own.
Prepare the cold toppings — dice the tomato, shred the lettuce, slice the avocado.
Build each bowl: rice on the bottom, then beans and corn, then the peppers and onion, then the cold toppings in their own sections.
Finish with cheese, sour cream, the rest of the coriander and a lime wedge on the side.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: A deconstructed plate: keep each element in its own corner of the bowl so a child who dislikes one thing can still eat everything else.
recipes.sourceNote: Written for Rasoi — lime and coriander stirred into the rice after cooking

recipes.title: Pasta with Hidden-Veggie Tomato Sauce

ingredients.note: passata, or 2 tins of chopped tomatoes blended
or a handful of fresh basil
1½ for the pasta water, ½ for the sauce
only if the tomatoes are sharp

steps: Warm 2 tbsp olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook 5 minutes until translucent — soft, not browned.
Add the sliced garlic and cook 1 minute, until it smells sweet. Browned garlic turns the whole sauce bitter.
Add the diced carrot and courgette with ¼ tsp salt and cook 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until the carrot is soft enough to crush against the pan.
Pour in 700 g passata, add 1½ tsp Italian seasoning, ¼ tsp black pepper and the remaining ¼ tsp salt, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer uncovered for 12 minutes, stirring occasionally. The sauce is ready when a spoon drawn through it leaves a channel for a second.
Taste. If it is sharp, add ½ tsp sugar — a small amount of sugar in tomato sauce is seasoning, not sweetening.
Blend the sauce smooth with a stick blender, right in the pan. This is what hides the vegetables.
Meanwhile bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil, add 1½ tsp salt, and cook 350 g pasta for one minute less than the packet says.
Scoop out a mugful of pasta water before draining. Starchy water is what makes the sauce cling.
Drain the pasta and return it to the pot with the sauce. Toss over low heat for 1 minute, loosening with pasta water a splash at a time until it coats every piece.
Serve with grated parmesan, and keep any leftover sauce — it freezes well for a night when nobody wants to cook.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Blending the sauce is the point: carrot and courgette disappear completely and it tastes sweeter than a plain tomato sauce. Keep a little pasta water to loosen it.
recipes.sourceNote: Written for Rasoi — soffritto method with the vegetables blended into the sauce

recipes.title: Cauliflower Mac & Cheese

ingredients.note: 1¼ for the water, ½ for the sauce
a scrape — the classic béchamel seasoning

steps: Bring a large pot of water to the boil and add 1¼ tsp salt.
Cook 300 g pasta for 2 minutes less than the packet says, adding the cauliflower florets for the last 5 minutes. One pot, both jobs.
While that cooks, melt 3 tbsp butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Whisk in 3 tbsp flour and cook for 2 minutes, whisking constantly. It should smell biscuity — that is the raw flour taste cooking out.
Pour in the warm milk a third at a time, whisking smooth after each addition before adding more. Adding it all at once is how lumps happen.
Simmer gently for 4–5 minutes, whisking, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Take the pan off the heat. Add ½ tsp salt, ¼ tsp black pepper and a scrape of nutmeg.
Add 200 g grated cheddar a handful at a time, stirring until each is melted. Off the heat is essential: boiled cheese sauce splits and goes oily.
Drain the pasta and cauliflower and fold them into the sauce, breaking up the softest florets with the spoon so they melt into it.
Serve as it is, or spread it in a dish, scatter over the parmesan and breadcrumbs and grill for 4 minutes until the top is spotted brown.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: The cauliflower cooks with the pasta and disappears into the sauce. Grate the cheese yourself — pre-grated cheese has starch on it and makes the sauce grainy.
recipes.sourceNote: Written for Rasoi — béchamel method, cheese added off the heat

recipes.title: Homemade Veggie Pizza

ingredients.note: shop-bought or your own, at room temperature

steps: Put a heavy baking tray or a pizza stone in the oven and heat it to the highest setting your oven has, at least 240°C. Give it a full 20 minutes to get properly hot.

Make the sauce without cooking it: mix 200 g passata with the crushed garlic, 1 tsp Italian seasoning, ¾ tsp salt, ¼ tsp pepper, 1 tbsp olive oil and the sugar if needed. An uncooked sauce tastes fresher after the fierce heat of the oven.
Slice the vegetables thinly — thick slices release water and make the middle soggy.
Divide the dough in two and stretch each piece on a floured sheet of baking paper to about 25 cm, leaving the rim slightly thicker.
Spread half the sauce on each base, leaving a 2 cm border, and go lightly: too much sauce is the most common home-pizza mistake.
Scatter over the mozzarella, then the vegetables. Cheese under the vegetables stops them drying out.
Slide the pizza, still on its paper, onto the hot tray. Bake 10–12 minutes, until the crust is blistered and the cheese is bubbling with brown spots.
Bake the second pizza the same way while the first one rests.
Brush the crust rim with the remaining olive oil, add the parmesan and the last ½ tsp Italian seasoning, and let it sit 2 minutes before cutting so the cheese sets.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Let each child top their own quarter. A hot tray or stone is what gives a crisp base at home — a cold tray makes the bottom soft and disappointing.
recipes.sourceNote: Written for Rasoi — hot-tray method with a no-cook tomato sauce

recipes.title: Vegetable Egg Fried Rice

ingredients.note: cooked and chilled overnight, about 4 cups
beaten with a pinch of salt
at the end, off the heat
rice vinegar if you have it
level — the soy sauce brings plenty

steps: Break up the cold rice with your fingers so there are no lumps. This takes two minutes and decides whether the dish is fried rice or rice pudding.
Line everything up beside the stove: beaten eggs, vegetables, aromatics, sauces. Once the wok is hot there is no time to chop.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok or your widest pan over the highest heat until it shimmers.
Pour in the beaten eggs and let them set for 20 seconds, then scramble them in big soft curds. Tip them out onto a plate while they are still slightly wet.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil, then the garlic, ginger and the white parts of the spring onions. Stir for 30 seconds — no longer, or the garlic burns.
Add the frozen vegetables and stir-fry 2 minutes until they are hot and any water has boiled off.
Add the rice and press it into the pan, then toss. Keep it moving for 3–4 minutes so it heats through and picks up a little colour.
Pour 2 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tsp vinegar around the edge of the pan rather than over the rice — it sizzles and caramelises instead of making things soggy.
Return the egg, add ½ tsp black pepper and ½ tsp salt, and toss everything together for 1 minute.
Turn off the heat, add 1 tsp sesame oil and the green parts of the spring onions, toss once and serve immediately.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Cold leftover rice is the secret — fresh rice steams and clumps. Scramble the egg separately so children who are unsure about egg can see exactly what is in it.
recipes.sourceNote: Written for Rasoi — day-old rice, high heat, everything prepped before the wok

recipes.title: Tofu & Broccoli Noodle Stir-Fry
steps: Press the tofu: wrap the block in a clean cloth, put a plate and a tin on top, and leave it 20 minutes. Water squeezed out now is flavour absorbed later.
Cut it into 2 cm cubes and toss with 1 tbsp cornstarch and ½ tsp salt — the coating is what makes the crust.
Mix the sauce in a cup: 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp vinegar, 1 tbsp grated ginger, half the garlic and 4 tbsp water.
Cook the noodles one minute short of the packet time, drain, rinse cold and toss with 1 tsp sesame oil.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wide pan on medium-high. Lay the tofu in one layer and leave it for 3 minutes without touching it — moving it early is why tofu sticks and falls apart.
Turn the cubes and brown the other sides, about 4 minutes in total, then lift them out.
Add the last 1 tbsp oil, the broccoli and the carrot, and stir-fry 3 minutes.
Add 3 tbsp water and cover for 2 minutes to steam the broccoli through, then uncover and let the water boil away.
Add the pepper and remaining garlic and stir-fry 1 minute.
Return the tofu, add the noodles and pour the sauce around the edge of the pan. Toss for 2 minutes until everything is glossy and the sauce clings.
Finish with ½ tsp black pepper and the toasted sesame seeds, and serve straight away.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Pressing and browning the tofu gives it a chewy edge rather than a wobbly one, which is usually the difference between eaten and pushed aside.
recipes.sourceNote: Written for Rasoi — pressed and seared tofu with a soy, honey and ginger glaze

recipes.title: Instant Pot Red Lentil Soup with Garlic Bread

ingredients.note: cloves: 3 for the soup, 2 for the bread
or water with a stock cube
juice, about 2 tbsp — do not skip this

steps: Rinse 250 g red lentils until the water runs clear. They cook down to nothing, so grit matters.
Set the Instant Pot to Sauté and warm 2 tbsp olive oil. Cook the onion, carrot and celery for 6 minutes until the onion is soft and translucent.
Add 3 minced garlic cloves and cook 1 minute.
Add 1½ tsp ground cumin, 1 tsp coriander powder, ½ tsp turmeric and ¼ tsp chilli powder and fry 1 minute, until the kitchen smells of cumin.
Add the tomatoes and cook 3 minutes until they break down.
Add the lentils, 1.2 litres stock, 1½ tsp salt and ½ tsp black pepper.
Cancel Sauté, close the lid and pressure cook on high for 8 minutes with a 10-minute natural release. On the stovetop, simmer covered for 25 minutes.
Blend about half the soup with a stick blender, leaving the rest with texture. Adjust with hot stock if it has gone too thick.
For the bread: mash 2 tbsp softened butter with the remaining 2 garlic cloves, crushed, spread it on the slices and grill for 3 minutes until the edges are crisp.
Stir 2 tbsp lemon juice into the soup off the heat and taste. Lentil soup without acid tastes flat, and the lemon is what wakes it up.
Serve in bowls with the coriander scattered over and the garlic bread alongside.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Blend half the soup and leave the rest chunky — smooth enough for a small child, with something to chew for everyone else. The garlic bread does the persuading.
recipes.sourceNote: Written for Rasoi — Middle Eastern style, finished with lemon and cumin

recipes.title: Veggie Hakka Noodles

ingredients.note: on the side for the adults
1 for the noodle water, ½ for the wok

steps: Bring a large pot of water to the boil with 1 tsp salt and cook the noodles for one minute less than the packet says, so they still have bite.
Drain, rinse under cold water to stop them cooking, and toss with 1 tsp sesame oil. This is what keeps them from welding together in the wok.
Cut the vegetables into matchsticks of about the same size while the noodles cool — in a stir-fry everything cooks in three minutes, so it all has to be the same thickness.
Heat 2½ tbsp oil in your widest pan over the highest heat until it just begins to smoke.
Add the garlic, ginger and spring onion whites and stir for 20 seconds.
Add the carrot and beans and stir-fry 2 minutes, keeping everything moving.
Add the pepper and cabbage and stir-fry 2 minutes more. The vegetables should still be bright and crunchy — this is not a curry.
Add the noodles and toss with two spatulas, lifting from the bottom, for 2 minutes.
Pour 2½ tbsp soy sauce and 2 tsp vinegar around the edge of the pan, add ¾ tsp black pepper and ½ tsp salt, and toss for another minute until everything is coated and glossy.
Turn off the heat, fold through the spring onion greens, and serve with sriracha on the side for whoever wants it.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Cut everything into matchsticks so it twirls onto a fork with the noodles. Keep the chilli sauce on the side and let each child add their own.
recipes.sourceNote: Written for Rasoi — Indo-Chinese method: par-cooked noodles, very high heat

recipes.title: Sheet-Pan Paneer Tikka & Veggies
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). A properly hot oven is what chars the edges instead of steaming everything.
Toast 1 tbsp besan in a dry pan for 1 minute until it smells nutty, then let it cool. Raw besan tastes chalky in a marinade.

Whisk 150 g thick yogurt with the toasted besan, 2 tbsp oil, 1 tsp ginger, 1 tsp garlic, 1 tsp chilli powder, ¼ tsp turmeric, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp crushed kasuri methi, 1¼ tsp salt and the lemon juice.
Cut the paneer, peppers, onion and cauliflower into pieces of roughly the same size so they finish together.
Fold the vegetables through the marinade first, then the paneer — paneer breaks if it is stirred too much, so add it last and turn gently.
Leave to marinate 15 minutes if you have time; an hour in the fridge is better.
Spread everything on a large lined tray in one layer with space between the pieces. A crowded tray steams; use two trays rather than piling it up.
Roast 15 minutes, then turn the pieces with a spatula.
Roast another 8–10 minutes, until the paneer is golden and the cauliflower has dark spots on its edges.
Sprinkle ½ tsp chaat masala over the hot tray and squeeze over a little more lemon.
Serve straight from the tray with warm naan and a bowl of plain yogurt.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Everything roasts on one tray, so the edges char slightly and taste sweet rather than spicy. Serve with naan and a bowl of yogurt for dipping.
recipes.sourceNote: Written for Rasoi — oven adaptation of the classic yogurt-and-besan tikka marinade

recipes.title: Dahi Aloo (Potatoes in Yogurt Gravy)

ingredients.note: small potatoes, boiled and peeled, halved
about 15 g, whisked into the yogurt

steps: Boil 500 g small potatoes until a knife slides in easily, about 15 minutes, then peel them and cut any large ones in half.
Whisk 400 g yogurt with 2 tbsp besan and 300 ml water until completely smooth. The besan is insurance: it holds the yogurt together when it heats.
Warm 1½ tbsp ghee in a pan. Add ¾ tsp cumin seeds and a pinch of asafoetida and let them sizzle 20 seconds.
Add 1 tsp grated ginger and the slit chilli and fry 30 seconds.
Turn the heat low and add ½ tsp turmeric, 1½ tsp coriander powder and ¼ tsp chilli powder. Fry for 30 seconds only — these burn fast in ghee.
Pour in the yogurt mixture and add 1¼ tsp salt, stirring constantly.
Keep stirring in one direction until it comes to a simmer. Do not walk away: yogurt that boils before it is stirred smooth will split.
Once simmering, add the potatoes and cook uncovered on low for 10 minutes, so the gravy thickens and the potatoes take on the flavour.
Crush a couple of potato halves against the side of the pan to thicken the gravy further.
Turn off the heat, stir in ½ tsp garam masala and the coriander, lift out the chilli, and serve with rice or puri.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Mild, creamy and almost sweet — a good one for a child who says everything is too spicy. Whisk besan into the yogurt so the gravy cannot split.
recipes.sourceNote: Written for Rasoi — the classic no-onion, no-garlic yogurt gravy

recipes.title: Instant Pot Quinoa Vegetable Pulao

ingredients.note: 1½ cups, rinsed in a fine sieve for a full minute

steps: Rinse 250 g quinoa in a fine sieve under cold running water for a full minute, rubbing it with your fingers. The bitter saponin coating is why quinoa gets rejected.
Set the Instant Pot to Sauté and warm 1½ tbsp ghee. Add ¾ tsp cumin seeds, the bay leaf and cardamom and let them sizzle 20 seconds.
Add the sliced onion and fry 4 minutes until soft and golden at the edges.
Stir in 1 tsp ginger, 1 tsp garlic and the slit chilli; cook 1 minute.
Add the frozen vegetables and ¼ tsp turmeric and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the drained quinoa and turn it through the spices for 1 minute so every grain is coated.
Pour in 375 ml water with 1¼ tsp salt — quinoa needs far less water than rice, about 1 part quinoa to 1¼ parts water.
Cancel Sauté, close the lid and pressure cook on high for 1 minute, then let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes. One minute is not a typo; quinoa cooks in the residual heat.
Open the pot: the grains should have uncurled little white tails. Fluff with a fork.
Stir in ¾ tsp garam masala, 1 tbsp lemon juice and the coriander, and serve with yogurt.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Rinsing the quinoa properly is the whole trick — unrinsed quinoa tastes soapy and children notice immediately. Serve with yogurt to soften the texture.
recipes.sourceNote: Written for Rasoi — pulao method adapted to quinoa's 1:1.25 water ratio

recipes.title: Sweet Potato & Black Bean Burgers

ingredients.note: one tin, drained, rinsed and dried well

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Prick the sweet potatoes and roast them whole for 40 minutes until completely soft, or microwave them for 8 minutes. Roasting drives off water; boiling adds it, and wet mixture means falling-apart burgers.
Scoop the flesh into a bowl and mash it. You want about 300 g.
Dry the drained beans on a cloth, then add them to the bowl and mash roughly, leaving about a third of them whole for texture.
Warm 1 tbsp olive oil in a pan and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, 1½ tsp cumin, 1 tsp coriander powder and ½ tsp chilli powder for 1 minute.
Scrape the onion mixture into the bowl with 60 g blitzed oats, 40 g breadcrumbs, 1¼ tsp salt and ½ tsp black pepper.
Mix with your hands until it holds together when squeezed. If it feels wet, add breadcrumbs a tablespoon at a time.
Shape into 4 patties about 2 cm thick, pressing them firmly, and chill for at least 15 minutes. This step is the difference between a burger and a hash.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a heavy pan on medium. Cook the patties 4–5 minutes on the first side without moving them, until a crust forms.
Turn once, carefully, and cook another 4 minutes. Add a slice of cheese for the last minute and cover so it melts.
Toast the buns cut-side down in the same pan for 1 minute.
Build with lettuce, tomato and ketchup, and serve immediately while the crust is still crisp.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Chilling the patties for 15 minutes is what stops them falling apart in the pan, which is the thing children remember about a homemade burger.
recipes.sourceNote: Written for Rasoi — roasted sweet potato base, bound with oats and breadcrumbs

recipes.title: Instant Pot Egg Curry with Rice
steps: Lower 6 eggs into boiling water and cook for 9 minutes, then move them straight into cold water for 5 minutes. Nine minutes gives a set yolk without the grey ring.
Peel the eggs and pat them dry. Prick each one two or three times with a fork so the gravy can get inside.
Warm 1 tsp ghee in the pot and roll the eggs around for 2 minutes until they blister and turn golden in patches. Lift them out.
Rinse 300 g rice until clear and simmer in 600 ml water with a pinch of salt: 12 minutes covered on low, then 5 minutes resting.
In the same pot, warm 2 tbsp oil. Add the bay leaf, cinnamon and cardamom and let them sizzle 20 seconds.
Add the chopped onion and fry 6–7 minutes, until golden and the raw smell has gone.
Stir in ½ tsp ginger and ½ tsp garlic; cook 1 minute.
Pour in the tomato purée with ½ tsp of the salt and cook 5–6 minutes, until it thickens and the oil separates at the edges.
Lower the heat and add ⅛ tsp turmeric, ½ tsp chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder and ½ tsp of the garam masala. Fry 2 minutes.
Add 300 ml water, the remaining ½ tsp salt and the sugar if using. Simmer covered for 8 minutes until the gravy thickens.
Slide the eggs in, crush ¼ tsp kasuri methi over the pot and simmer 3 minutes, spooning gravy over them.
Turn off the heat, add the last ¼ tsp garam masala and the coriander, and halve the eggs as you serve them over the rice.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Halve the eggs before serving so a child can see what they are eating, and give them the yolk-side up in a little gravy over rice.
recipes.sourceNote: Adapted from Swasthi's Punjabi Egg Curry (Indian Healthy Recipes)

recipes.title: Mild Vegetable Korma

ingredients.note: fresh or frozen, for the paste

steps: Blend 12 cashews and 4 tbsp coconut with 90 ml water into a completely smooth paste. Any grittiness here shows up in the finished gravy, so give it a full minute.
Cut the potato, carrot and beans into 1 cm dice and break the cauliflower into small florets, so everything cooks in the same time.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wide pan. Add the bay leaf, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves and ½ tsp cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add the chopped onion and fry 4–5 minutes until soft and pale gold.
Stir in 1 tsp ginger and 1 tsp garlic; cook 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and ½ tsp of the salt and cook 5 minutes until mushy.
Turn the heat low and add ¼ tsp turmeric, 1 tsp chilli powder and ¾ tsp of the garam masala. Fry 2 minutes.
Add the cashew-coconut paste and fry for 3 minutes, stirring constantly — it catches easily and burnt cashew paste cannot be rescued.
Add all the vegetables except the peas, turn them through the masala for 2 minutes, then pour in 400 ml hot water with the remaining ¾ tsp salt.
Simmer covered for 15 minutes, until a potato cube gives to a knife with no resistance.
Stir in the frozen peas and simmer 3 minutes more, uncovered, so the gravy thickens to the point where it coats the vegetables.
Turn off the heat, stir in the remaining ½ tsp garam masala and the coriander, and serve with roti or rice.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: The cashew-coconut paste makes it creamy and sweet rather than hot — the chilli powder is there for colour. Serve with soft roti so it can be scooped.
recipes.sourceNote: Adapted from Swasthi's Veg Kurma (Indian Healthy Recipes)

recipes.title: Green Monster Smoothie
steps: Add everything to Vitamix, liquids first.
Blend on high 45 s until silky.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Bright green and sweet — call it 'monster juice'; spinach is undetectable.

recipes.title: Berry Oat Smoothie
steps: Blend everything 45 s on high.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Purple = popular. Freeze extra into popsicles.

recipes.title: Mango Lassi
steps: Blend mango, yogurt, milk, cardamom until smooth.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Use frozen mango chunks off-season.

recipes.title: Carrot Beet Orange Smoothie
steps: Blend with 200 ml water on high 60 s (Vitamix handles raw carrot and beet).
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Hot-pink colour sells it; add more orange if too earthy.

recipes.title: Ghee-Roasted Makhana
steps: Roast makhana in ghee on low 6–8 min until crisp.
Toss with salt and turmeric.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Crunchy like popcorn; stores a week in a jar.

recipes.title: Rainbow Fruit Chaat
steps: Chop fruit into bite-size pieces.
Toss with lemon; chaat masala for the grown-ups' portion.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Toothpick 'kebabs' make it a game.

recipes.title: Veggie Sticks with Hummus
steps: Blend chickpeas, sesame, lemon, garlic, oil, salt + 50 ml water in Vitamix until creamy.
Cut veg into sticks; serve with hummus and pita triangles.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Dipping is the hook; start with cucumber and carrot.

recipes.title: 3-Ingredient Oat Banana Cookies
steps: Mash bananas; stir in oats, chocolate chips or raisins.
Drop spoonfuls on a tray; bake 180 °C 12–15 min.
recipes.kidFriendlyNote: Kids can mix and scoop; no added sugar.
